overview: The Dashashrutaskandha is a significant Jain text, primarily associated with the Svetambara tradition. It is part of the canonical scriptures known as the Agamas. The text is believed to have been composed by the revered Acharya Bhadrabahu. The Dashashrutaskandha consists of ten chapters, each detailing various aspects of Jain philosophy, ethics, and monastic conduct. It serves as a guide for monks and nuns in their spiritual and daily lives, emphasizing the importance of discipline, non-violence, truthfulness, and the pursuit of knowledge. The text is also valuable for lay practitioners seeking a deeper understanding of Jain tenets, providing insights into the path of liberation and the intricacies of karma theory.

primary_sources.title: Dashashrutaskandha
primary_sources.author: Acharya Bhadrabahu
primary_sources.notes: The text is part of the Svetambara Agamas and is used in monastic training. It is known for its detailed exposition of monastic rules and spiritual practices.

misconceptions.myth: The Dashashrutaskandha is solely a historical document.
misconceptions.reality: While it has historical significance, the Dashashrutaskandha is actively used in religious study and practice within the Jain community.
